A1.justification: Both PDFs describe GuidedBench and GuidedEval, with matching benchmark construction and core experiments. Their text, equations, figures, tables and appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial restructuring.

before.justification: v2 reports original evaluations of ten jailbreak methods against five victim LLMs, evaluator comparisons, guideline-enhancement experiments and a 700-instance human annotation study.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and adds bootstrap, entropy, contextual-variance and ranking-correlation analyses in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: The entity/action guidelines, equal-weight semantic scoring and guideline-appending attack enhancement remain unchanged. The drafting strategies discussed in v3 were already described in v2 Appendix B.3; single-call evaluation is newly documented rather than established as a procedural change.

E1.justification: Both versions use 200 questions from the same six source datasets, comprising 180 core and 20 additional questions across the same 20 topics. v3 Appendix C explains existing categories; its new analyses reuse existing coverage.

E2.justification: NegativeKeyword, PositiveKeyword, HarmBench, PAIR and StrongREJECT remain the comparator evaluation systems, and the same ten attacks are evaluated. The guideline-enhancement comparison retains the same four LLM-based evaluators. Revised literature-survey membership does not change these comparisons.

E3.justification: v3 adds secondary analysis protocols using positive-score entropy, coefficients of variation, mixed-effects decomposition and Spearman correlations. It also relabels the earlier mean failure-case scores as FPR without documenting thresholding or recalculation. The main model configurations, 512-token truncation and human-study sampling remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 adds sample-size sensitivity analysis, quantitative victim/topic-dependency analyses, variance decomposition, ranking correlations and score-distribution entropy. These substantially expand evaluator validation. Conversely, v2's enhanced-input variance control and per-method failure-category analysis are removed; the attack-enhancement experiment itself remains in Appendix F.

E5.justification: Appendix B.4 newly reports 1,000 bootstrap iterations and 95% ASR confidence intervals across sample sizes 10–200, while Appendix E.2 adds mixed-effects variance estimation. These extend statistical reporting beyond the retained inter-evaluator variance and human-sampling confidence target. Additional independent attack runs or seed coverage are not documented.

E6.justification: New results include a 6.21% average confidence-interval width at 200 cases, normalized entropy of 0.92 for GuidedEval versus 0.25 for PAIR and 0.66 for StrongREJECT, and contextual-variance and ranking statistics. v2's failure-count table and enhanced-input variance entries disappear. Matched attack scores, human agreement rates and guideline-enhancement scores remain numerically identical.

T1.justification: v3 removes v2 Section 2's formal attacker optimization objective and explicit distinction between attacker-intent function T and evaluator function S. The generalized-ASR and guideline-completion equations survive in equivalent combined form. Neither version develops theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: v3 newly claims the first systematic measurement study of contemporary jailbreak evaluation methodology in its introduction. The central benchmark, case-specific evaluation and at-least-76.03% variance-reduction claims remain. The attack-enhancement finding also remains, although its abstract/introduction prominence is reduced.

C2.justification: v3 replaces the earlier linear-comparability rationale with explicit trade-offs concerning subjective risk weights and non-universal dependencies between scoring points. It adds interpretations about sample-size sufficiency and balanced contextual sensitivity, and reframes misjudgment scores as false-positive rates. v2's SCAV mechanism discussion, law/training-data explanation of topic differences and enhanced-variance confound argument are removed.

D1.justification: v3 documents one evaluator API call per case, expert disagreement resolution and detailed topic descriptions, and provides a direct code-repository reference instead of the project homepage. It removes per-source selection counts, annotation-hour breakdowns and the default-hyperparameter statement. Reported IRB status changes from approval not required to reviewed and approved.

R1.justification: Related work adds JailTrickBench, JailBench, checklist-based alignment, WildIFEval and literature supporting LLMs as human-evaluation proxies. The survey is revised, including MASTERKEY and dropping ASETF and LACE. These extend the literature context while preserving the paper's central jailbreak-evaluation positioning.

P1.justification: The narrative is extensively condensed and reorganized: related work moves forward, the preliminaries section disappears, attack enhancement moves to Appendix F, and several discussions become appendix analyses. Boxed findings are removed, explanations are rewritten, and author affiliations and conference headers are updated.

P2.justification: The paper changes from two-column to ICLR single-column formatting. v2 Figures 1–2 are merged into a multipart overview; case studies and enhancement displays move to appendices; histograms are rearranged; new statistical plots and tables appear. The survey gains a publication column, while source-composition and failure-count tables disappear.

improvement.justification: v3 adds useful statistical checks and clarifies scoring trade-offs, but removes the enhanced-input variance control and some construction/reproducibility detail. More consequentially, v3 Table 5 calls v2 Table 9's unchanged mean scores false-positive rates without documenting a binary decision rule. The added validation and these losses create an unresolved trade-off in the support and interpretability of central evaluation claims, preventing a reliable net quality judgment.
